newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 20.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Amnuay Viravan's role challenged by Chatichai. Tough conditions, including Chart Pattana's preference that someone other than Amnuay heads the ecnomomic team, stalled talks yesterday on the allocation of key portfolios among the New Aspiration-led alliance. Chart Pattana made its position clear to Chavalit Yongchaiyudh in the second round of talks at the home of Chart Pattana leader Chatichai Choonhavan.

A Chart Pattana source said since the party is to take some ecnomic portfolios, it was not keen on being under Amnuay. The stand goes against the stated intention of Chavalit to make Amnuay finance minister and economic supremo. (BANGKOK POST)

- Tourist seeks compensation of 177 million baht. An American tourist who became physically disabled after being hit by a bus in Bangkok last year has sued the bus driver, the bus service operation and the Bangkok Mass Transportation Authority, demanding 177.8 million baht in compensation. (THE NATION)

- Chart Pattana key to stable coalition. New Aspiration Party leader Chavalit will have a very stable coalition government compared with the two previous administrations. The Chart Pattana Party, the second largest partner in the coalition, will not pose a threat to Chavalit's premiership if he manages to please it with the proper quota of cabinet seats. (BANGKOK POST)

- Local and foreign businessmen in Thailand doubt Chavalit Yongchaiyudh's government can solve the country's enconomic problems, a Business Post survey shows. They are also worried that the Chavalit-led coalition will be corrupt as many MPs will be eager to recoup money spent on what has been called country's dirtiest election.

Of 100 Bangkok businessmen questioned, only a few said they were satisfied with the new coalition of six parties. Some doubted the economic tem led by Amnuay Viravan would be given full independence and authority over economic policies and suggested political intervention would again cause problems. (BANGKOK POST)

- Banks cut lending rates to help the Bank of Thailand boost confidence. At least five large commercial banks have approved BOT policy by agreeing to reduce the minimum lending rate (MLR) by the end of the year to stimulate the economy, BOT executives said. Siam Commercial Bank yesterday cut its minimum retail rate by a quarter of a percent to 13.5 percent, effective immediately. BOT governor Rerngchai Maraknond said commercial banks and the BOT were trying to pull down interest rates to boost investment without undermining Thailand's ecnomic stability. (THE NATION).

- Investor confidence must be restored quickly, according to the Board of Trade. The board proposed new guidelines to help the new government repair the economy, which it conceded had been damaged by the previous administration. Only those with a wealth of experience in economic fields should receive key economic posts, it said. (BANGKOK POST)
